newsitem.title: USA: Perry for more nuclear cuts after START-2 ratified.
newsitem.headline: Perry for more nuclear cuts after START-2 ratified.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Perry, responding to calls by two former U.S. generals for the elimination of nuclear weapons, said on Wednesday that further American reductions should be made only if Russia's parliament ratifies the START-2 nuclear arms reduction treaty.
"I do not believe in unilaterally eliminating our nuclear weapons. You cannot uninvent the nuclear bomb," Perry told reporters.

"While I push for very deep and very fast reductions, I want to do them in a way which takes into account the nuclear weapons of other nation, in particular the present level of nuclear weapons in Russia," Perry said aboard his aircraft as he ended a globe-circling trip.

Earlier in the day, Retired Air Force Gen. Lee Butler, who was commander of U.S. nuclear forces until two years ago, and retired Army Gen. Andrew Goodpaster, who was NATO's commander from 1969 to 1974, said the process of eliminating nuclear arms should begin now with deep cuts.

The two former generals said complete elimination of the world's nuclear weapons would probably take decades but the United States and Russia should take the lead in reducing weapons numbers to "very low levels."

"I would not recommend to the president to cut the U.S. forces down to Start-2 levels until we can get that ratification in the Duma," Perry said of resistance in the lower house of Russia's parliament to approve the treaty despite its ratification this year by the U.S. Senate.
The treaty would slice U.S. and Russian long-range nuclear warheads to fewer than 3,500 each by the year 2003. START-2, signed in 1993, would take stockpiles down to a third of Cold War levels.
"Gen. Butler and Gen. Goodpaster are good friends and have been for many years and I have great regard for them personally and great respect for them professionally," Perry said.
But he added that the United States should "push very, very hard" to get Russian ratification "and I am still optimistic that we will succeed."
"So I see this as a step-by-step process, the next step of which is to go to Start-2."

Perry said that the number of U.S. short-range, or theatre, nuclear weapons have been reducted by 90 percent in the last six or seven years and that strategic arsenals in both the United States and Russia have been cut in half.
"If we can get Start-2 approved we will cut them (strategic warheads) in half again," he said.

He said that the United States should agree to start quickly on START-3 immediately after START-2 is ratified in order to cut strategic nuclear warheads by half again and also assuage Russian fears that the United States would have a nuclear edge after START-2.
"I think START-2 and START-3 are bold steps and I do not have in my mind a bolder step than that for getting the reduction," he said.
